Having reached the practical limits of medium sized cooling systems, the designers of caseless ammunition blazed a path into larger weapons with the Storm Needler's advanced nano coolant recyclers, per-barrel magnetized rifling, and automated operation. An intelligent autoloader unpacks and loads just the right amount of ammunition from the magazines, allowing for prolonged operation provided the host ship has adequate flux capacity.
name: Storm Needler

description:
"If our particle accelerators could do that, it'd be like peeking into the mind of God."
- intercept, [REDACTED]
name: Pseudoparticle Jet

description:
"[Best match: 'Light Mass Driver weapon system (obsolete)'  / abbreviated: true / show partial match: true / warnings: Variant contains unlicensed modifications. Variant displays unregistered production ID. Variant may be in violation of Domain Technological Safety Standards.]

"...which fires a dense, partly ferrous hypervelocity projectile which delivers a respectable kinetic payload for its class."

"...is a militarized version of the Stencor civilian Mk.III Linear Catapult favored by frontier mining combines. Earned a poor reputation due to accidents caused by unlicensed nanofactured copies.
- Results compiled from 'The Authorized Encyclopedia of Early Weapon Systems of the Domain Armada, 43rd edition'
name: Light Mass Driver

description:
"A gamma ray burst preceded the discharge of unprecedented stream of... we must admit, EM sensors could not penetrate the plasma sheath and the gravimetric suite could not be calibrated under... yes, of course. My apologies. The physics team speculates ejecta is a stream of near-c charged matter-antimatter pseudoparticles annihilating in-situ in a... controlled, or perhaps semi-stable vortex. The baryonic asymmetry is unusual, to say the least."
- intercept, [REDACTED]
customPrimary: Produces explosions that deal up to 100 points of energy damage to all nearby targets, including the one being hit by the beam.
name: Abyssal Glare

description: This dumb-fire rocket was ubiquitous in the pre-Collapse Persean Sector due to applications pioneered by asteroid miners. The go-to strike weapon of the desperately under-equipped, the Hammer is often employed by poor independent militias, Pirates, and particularly the Luddic Path. This has led to the mildly blasphemous alternative name for the weapon, "Ludd's Hammer".
name: Hammer-class Torpedo (Single)

description:
"Previously undifferentiated autonomous fragments are re-assigned from the structure of the host vessel itself to replenish the standing cloud, from which they can be assigned into loosely organized strike-groups. The key element appears to be this - I'll designate it - a specialized systems node. We speculate that it is a distributed processing/communication cluster, one of several you will see highlighted on the hull, here. These appear to coordinate, possibly initiate and delegate, hostile behavior by elements of the semi-autonomous swarm."
- SEALED HOLO REPORT to be submitted to the Director of Special Acquisitions ONLY
customPrimary: Requires the %s hullmod and uses %s fragments per swarm launched. Can control up to %s swarms concurrently, but will wait to launch new swarms until the existing ones are depleted.
customAncillary: This weapon can not be fired manually and will always launch swarms as soon as it is possible to do so.
name: Swarm Launcher

damageType.description: 25% vs shields and armor, 100% vs hull

description:
A bulky energy weapon from an early epoch, the TPC is built directly into the Onslaught's hull to provide overwhelming frontal firepower.

Designed before modular energy weapons were universally trusted by Domain Armada procurement committees, this weapon was coded into the Onslaught's blueprint because no other hull of the time was capable of supplying required power.

Even though it's outperformed by some of the later epoch modular designs, the Thermal Pulse Cannon remains an integral part of the Onslaught's arsenal.
name: Thermal Pulse Cannon

description:
A huge, long-range flak cannon. The Heavy Adjudicator must be built into the hull of the Onslaught Mk.I due to the extreme bulk of the ammunition feed and recoil systems. Fills space with an astounding storm of shrapnel at great range - any fighter, missile, or armor-stripped ship is doomed if it finds itself within this zone of death.

The question remains, what purpose was such a dedicated weapon designed for before the rise of mobile forge-compatible strike fighter doctrine?
customPrimary:
Each shell has a proximity fuse and deals damage over a wide area when it explodes.

Will target missiles if no other targets are in range.
name: Heavy Adjudicator

damageType.description: 25% vs shields and armor, 100% vs hull

name: Base ModSpec
descFirstPara: A collection of notes, guidelines, and practical examples that enable one to adapt and apply this modification to various hulls.
desc: A collection of notes, guidelines, and practical examples that enable one to adapt and apply this modification to various hulls.

name: Corrupted Nanoforge
descFirstPara: A powerful and versatile manufacturing "black box", capable of building itself out to an industrial scale, given the necessary raw materials and human assistance.
desc:
A powerful and versatile manufacturing "black box", capable of building itself out to an industrial scale, given the necessary raw materials and human assistance.

This one has seen better days, and is incapable of reliably producing defect-free components. Nonetheless, having access to a nanoforge at all is a step up as far as starship construction goes.

name: Pristine Nanoforge
descFirstPara: A powerful and versatile manufacturing "black box", capable of building itself out to an industrial scale, given the necessary raw materials and human assistance.
desc:
A powerful and versatile manufacturing "black box", capable of building itself out to an industrial scale, given the necessary raw materials and human assistance.

This one is good as new, at least according to its on-board diagnostics. In practice, getting defect-free starship components is still a challenge given the overall state of manufacturing in the Sector, but this nanoforge is as good as it gets.

name: Synchrotron Core
descFirstPara: A specialized nanoforge, loaded with firmware and seed nano-tech to build itself out into a Synchrotron that allows industrial-scale antimatter production.
desc: A specialized nanoforge, loaded with firmware and seed nano-tech to build itself out into a Synchrotron that allows industrial-scale antimatter production.

name: Orbital Fusion Lamp
descFirstPara: A miniaturized, variable-output fusion reactor capable of providing ample light and heat to a planet.
desc:
A miniaturized, variable-output fusion reactor capable of providing ample light and heat to a planet.

Safe operation requires prodigious quantities of volatiles. If the demand is not met, the reactor suffers from potentially hazardous instability, which may lead to an uncontrolled surge in output. Litigation over whether this device is of inherently unsafe design or simply used unsafely were ongoing in Domain courts at the time of the Collapse.

name: Hypershunt Tap
descFirstPara: A miniaturized wormhole interface which can be activated to tap into a nearby coronal hypershunt, providing a colony with virtually unlimited power.
desc:
A miniaturized wormhole interface which can be activated to tap into a nearby coronal hypershunt, providing a colony with virtually unlimited power.

Operation requires industrial quantities of transplutonics, which are at first used to open the wormhole, and then - once the power drawn becomes self-sustaining - is consumed in a complicated ablative process which maintains wormhole stability. Any interruption in supply requires a full shutdown of the tap.

name: Autonomous Mantle Bore
descFirstPara: While it is believed there are no functional control override units remaining in the Sector, the bore itself is capable of independent - if sometimes unpredictable - operation. Automatic-mode failsafes preclude its use on habitable worlds.
desc: While it is believed there are no functional control override units remaining in the Sector, the bore itself is capable of independent - if sometimes unpredictable - operation. Automatic-mode failsafes preclude its use on habitable worlds.

name: Catalytic Core
descFirstPara: Vastly improves the effectiveness of refining operations by way of a surprising quirk of osmosis physics. Operation requires access to vacuum on a scale difficult to achieve on planets with significant atmospheric pressure.
desc: Vastly improves the effectiveness of refining operations by way of a surprising quirk of osmosis physics. Operation requires access to vacuum on a scale difficult to achieve on planets with significant atmospheric pressure.

name: Soil Nanites
descFirstPara: Enables soil enrichment and recovery at a rate far beyond that at which unaided natural processes perform. Domain Nanite Safety Regulation 4324, subsection 81 prohibits use on worlds with transplutonic ore or volatiles deposits, and unfortunately the built-in failsafe appears to be functional.
desc: Enables soil enrichment and recovery at a rate far beyond that at which unaided natural processes perform. Domain Nanite Safety Regulation 4324, subsection 81 prohibits use on worlds with transplutonic ore or volatiles deposits, and unfortunately the built-in failsafe appears to be functional.

name: Biofactory Embryo
descFirstPara: A dizzying array of consumer goods can be grown rather than manufactured. The fully-extruded biofactory only thrives in the delicate balance of sunlight, soil nutrients, and atmospheric conditions a habitable world can provide. Attempts to mimic these conditions in artificial environments always fail, causing the factory to sicken, presumably due to a genetically encoded failsafe.
desc: A dizzying array of consumer goods can be grown rather than manufactured. The fully-extruded biofactory only thrives in the delicate balance of sunlight, soil nutrients, and atmospheric conditions a habitable world can provide. Attempts to mimic these conditions in artificial environments always fail, causing the factory to sicken, presumably due to a genetically encoded failsafe.

name: Fullerene Spool
descFirstPara: An ultra-strong carbon nanomesh cable that is key to the construction of a space elevator. Greatly improves the efficiency of logistics between the surface of a planet and low orbit.
desc: An ultra-strong carbon nanomesh cable that is key to the construction of a space elevator. Greatly improves the efficiency of logistics between the surface of a planet and low orbit.

name: Plasma Dynamo
descFirstPara: The superconductor-flanged centerpiece of an industrial system which creates a planetary-scale plasma net that enables efficient, spectacular extraction of volatiles from the atmosphere of a suitable gas giant.
desc: The superconductor-flanged centerpiece of an industrial system which creates a planetary-scale plasma net that enables efficient, spectacular extraction of volatiles from the atmosphere of a suitable gas giant.

name: Cryoarithmetic Engine
descFirstPara: A quantum computer that violates the second law of thermodynamics by getting colder instead of hotter while performing computations.
desc:
A quantum computer that violates the second law of thermodynamics by getting colder instead of hotter while performing computations.

A massive, planet-wide network of tendrils - ending in heatsinks - extrudes itself, using heat to fuel growth and continued computation. The hotter the planet surface, the more effective the computation engine. The unrivaled processing capacity is a boon to logistical and strategic planning.

name: Combat Drone Replicator
descFirstPara: Mass-produces a number of drone variants, all suited to various tasks related to planetary defense against raids and invasions, as well as local security actions.
desc:
Mass-produces a number of drone variants, all suited to various tasks related to planetary defense against raids and invasions, as well as local security actions.

Its use was banned by the Domain many cycles prior to the Collapse, so it's surprising to find a working example in the Persean Sector.

name: Dealmaker Holosuite
descFirstPara: Generates an interactive environment designed to stimulate negotiations with prospective business partners. Additionally, the self-adapting microemotion smart sensor systems built into such high-end VR suites  allow real-time tracking of the veracity of expression, providing a technically ethical advantage in business dealings to the facility operator.
desc:
Generates an interactive environment designed to stimulate negotiations with prospective business partners. Additionally, the self-adapting microemotion smart sensor systems built into such high-end VR suites  allow real-time tracking of the veracity of expression, providing a technically ethical advantage in business dealings to the facility operator.  

The built-in marketing materials are keen to emphasize that this is not an AI, but merely a sophisticated weighted network in full compliance with the relevant Domain regulations.

name: Low Tech Blueprint Package
descFirstPara: Enables heavy industry to construct the more common ship hulls, weapons, and fighter LPCs from the "low tech" school of design.
desc: Enables heavy industry to construct the more common ship hulls, weapons, and fighter LPCs from the "low tech" school of design.

name: Midline Blueprint Package
descFirstPara: Enables heavy industry to construct the more common ship hulls, weapons, and fighter LPCs from the "midline" school of design.
desc: Enables heavy industry to construct the more common ship hulls, weapons, and fighter LPCs from the "midline" school of design.

name: High Tech Blueprint Package
descFirstPara: Enables heavy industry to construct the more common ship hulls, weapons, and fighter LPCs from the "high tech" school of design.
desc: Enables heavy industry to construct the more common ship hulls, weapons, and fighter LPCs from the "high tech" school of design.

name: Missile Blueprint Package
descFirstPara: Enables heavy industry to construct a range of the more common missile weapons.
desc: Enables heavy industry to construct a range of the more common missile weapons.

name: Pirate Blueprint Package
descFirstPara: A collection of hacks, after-market modification specs, and partially successful attempts at corrupted blueprint recovery. Enables heavy industry to construct the low quality but combat-capable hulls more commonly used by pirates and other undesirables.
desc: A collection of hacks, after-market modification specs, and partially successful attempts at corrupted blueprint recovery. Enables heavy industry to construct the low quality but combat-capable hulls more commonly used by pirates and other undesirables.

name: Luddic Path Blueprint Package
descFirstPara: A collection of hacks and after-market modification specs that enables heavy industry to construct the hulls more commonly used by members of the Luddic Path.
desc: A collection of hacks and after-market modification specs that enables heavy industry to construct the hulls more commonly used by members of the Luddic Path.

name: Luddic Church Blueprint Package
descFirstPara: A collection of hacks and after-market modification specs that enables heavy industry to construct hulls bearing Luddic Church markings. Since the modifications are cosmetic in nature, the hulls produced are otherwise pristine.
desc: A collection of hacks and after-market modification specs that enables heavy industry to construct hulls bearing Luddic Church markings. Since the modifications are cosmetic in nature, the hulls produced are otherwise pristine.

name: XIV Battlegroup Blueprint Package
descFirstPara: A set of blueprints that enable heavy industry to produce the near-legendary hulls employed by the Hegemony-founding XIV Battlegroup. The continued existence - and location - of these blueprints is subject of many rumors.
desc: A set of blueprints that enable heavy industry to produce the near-legendary hulls employed by the Hegemony-founding XIV Battlegroup. The continued existence - and location - of these blueprints is subject of many rumors.

name: Hegemony Auxiliary Blueprints
descFirstPara: A collection of modified blueprints that bring several civilian craft up to mil-spec or simply add Hegemony markings. Created shortly after the Collapse, some of these blueprints improve hull performance without the increased incidence of d-mods associated with later blueprint hacking efforts.
desc: A collection of modified blueprints that bring several civilian craft up to mil-spec or simply add Hegemony markings. Created shortly after the Collapse, some of these blueprints improve hull performance without the increased incidence of d-mods associated with later blueprint hacking efforts.

name: Base Ship Blueprint
descFirstPara: Enables heavy industry to construct ship hulls described by this blueprint.
desc: Enables heavy industry to construct ship hulls described by this blueprint.

name: Base Weapon Blueprint
descFirstPara: Enables heavy industry to construct ship weapons described by this blueprint.
desc: Enables heavy industry to construct ship weapons described by this blueprint.

name: Base Fighter Blueprint
descFirstPara: Enables heavy industry to construct fighter LPCs described by this blueprint.
desc: Enables heavy industry to construct fighter LPCs described by this blueprint.

name: Base Industry Blueprint
descFirstPara: Contains the technological specifications needed to construct a planet-side industry or structure.
desc: Contains the technological specifications needed to construct a planet-side industry or structure.

name: Janus Device
descFirstPara: This is the first generation Janus Device created by Elissa Zal based on the theories developed by Scylla Coureuse, among others.
desc:
This is the first generation Janus Device created by Elissa Zal based on the theories developed by Scylla Coureuse, among others.

While integrated with a hyperdrive this device allows a hyperwave pulse tuned to the unique resonant signatures of two Gates to be transmitted into a Gate aperture. After a tremendous energy input which requires a great quantity of fuel to generate, a temporary link between those Gates is created. One ship or fleet may then transit the Gate network.

name: Planetkiller
descFirstPara: A specialized warhead capable of sundering a world. Operating principles are only dimly understood and are thought to involve utilizing the world's spin and some form of resonance.
desc:
A specialized warhead capable of sundering a world. Operating principles are only dimly understood and are thought to involve utilizing the world's spin and some form of resonance.

This one is safed and requires authorization codes, possibly long-lost, to become anything more than a complicated, but completely inert piece of machinery.

name: Topographic Data
descFirstPara: This secure TriPad contains a recent database which holds detailed scans and analyses of the hyperspace topography in the Persean Sector, organized according to traditional guidelines set by the Domain Explorarium. Data such as this is an essential element to successful expeditions outside the core worlds.
desc: This secure TriPad contains a recent database which holds detailed scans and analyses of the hyperspace topography in the Persean Sector, organized according to traditional guidelines set by the Domain Explorarium. Data such as this is an essential element to successful expeditions outside the core worlds.

name: Wormhole Anchor
descFirstPara: Unfamiliar to the contemporary Persean Sector, this technology saw use by the Domain Explorarium during an era of greatness long past. Can be used to create a wormhole terminus at a stable location.
desc:
Unfamiliar to the contemporary Persean Sector, this technology saw use by the Domain Explorarium during an era of greatness long past. Can be used to create a wormhole terminus at a stable location.

Initial activation requires antimatter in the form of starship fuel. Requires at least one other active and synchronized terminus to use.

name: Wormhole Scanner
descFirstPara: A Domain-era artifact which allows a fleet to navigate a natural wormhole, following its many twists, turns, and shifts through higher dimensions. A fleet entering a wormhole without a scanner would never be seen again, at least not as a coherent collection of baryonic matter.
desc:
A Domain-era artifact which allows a fleet to navigate a natural wormhole, following its many twists, turns, and shifts through higher dimensions. A fleet entering a wormhole without a scanner would never be seen again, at least not as a coherent collection of baryonic matter.

The operating principles can only be dimly guessed at given the present state-of-the-art in the Persean Sector.

name: Fragment Fabricator
descFirstPara: Unfamiliar technology which nonetheless shares design principles with ancient Domain engineering standards. Various self-modifying adapters accept energy and forge-stock input. There is no command interface. Attempts to interfere with workings provoke aggressive cannibalizing self-repair mechanisms; a major attempt to dismantle the unit would risk self-destruction.
desc:
Unfamiliar technology which nonetheless shares design principles with ancient Domain engineering standards. Various self-modifying adapters accept energy and forge-stock input. There is no command interface. Attempts to interfere with workings provoke aggressive cannibalizing self-repair mechanisms; a major attempt to dismantle the unit would risk self-destruction.

This is clearly a fabricator, because when the inputs are fed, it produces Fragment units, each of which is formed of a unique arrangement of fractal components but which is functionally similar, with slight allowance for scale. Simple on an individual level, the fragments exhibit sophisticated emergent behavior in groups.

name: Threat Processing Unit
descFirstPara: A basic, modular computational unit. These seem to be employed in large numbers to support the various functions of Threat vessels. Not fully understood, but clearly well below the threshold for being considered an artificial intelligence of any level.
desc: A basic, modular computational unit. These seem to be employed in large numbers to support the various functions of Threat vessels. Not fully understood, but clearly well below the threshold for being considered an artificial intelligence of any level.

name: Shrouded Substrate
descFirstPara: Anomalous exotic matter held in semi-stable stasis using makeshift containment units. It is recommended to employ hazardous material handling protocols class 6, 7, 9, and 13. Cursory investigation suggests applications in energy projection.
desc: Anomalous exotic matter held in semi-stable stasis using makeshift containment units. It is recommended to employ hazardous material handling protocols class 6, 7, 9, and 13. Cursory investigation suggests applications in energy projection.

name: Shrouded Thunderhead
descFirstPara: "This self-sustaining action produces massive energy differentials which are periodically discharged toward its, um, target. I'd never have said a storm could be evil, but now..."
desc:
"This self-sustaining action produces massive energy differentials which are periodically discharged toward its, um, target. I'd never have said a storm could be evil, but now..."

- intercepted audio log, speaker unknown

name: Shrouded Mantle
descFirstPara: "We can't store energy forever in this theoretical, pretend-plasma. It'll have to go somewhere."
desc:
"We can't store energy forever in this theoretical, pretend-plasma. It'll have to go somewhere."

"-Invert the polarity of the flux converters and flicker the drive field. Boom, a gentle bump to local time-space. By which I mean the ship itself."

"If it works."

name: Shrouded Lens
descFirstPara: "Spin it up during combat maneuvers, adjusting the frequency of the 'probes' adapted from drive-field stabilizers. It would create hyperspace fractures which would cause terrible damage to n-space structures. Starships, for instance."
desc: "Spin it up during combat maneuvers, adjusting the frequency of the 'probes' adapted from drive-field stabilizers. It would create hyperspace fractures which would cause terrible damage to n-space structures. Starships, for instance."

description: Assorted supplies required by ships and crew, ranging from rations and uniforms to munitions, spare parts, microfab feedstock, and prefab components.
name: Supplies

description: Standard starship fuel on which interstellar civilization relies. Composed of antimatter trapped in fullerene shells mixed in a semi-stable foam with heavy isotopes of hydrogen. Fairly safe.
name: Fuel

description: Skilled personnel experienced in the maintenance and day-to-day operation of spaceships and smaller ground-based installations.
name: Crew

description: Heavily armed and equipped with powered armor, marines specialize in planetside operations such as raids.
name: Marines

description: Various food products, preserved and packaged for export. Guaranteed shelf-life of no fewer than five Domain-standard years.
name: Food

description: Bulk complex carbon-based molecules and derivatives thereof with applications in plastics, fuels, solvents, polymers, food products, biotech, life support, and a vast array of other necessities.
name: Organics

description: Rare isotopes of lighter elements - such as deuterium - with critical applications in fuel production and other advanced industrial processes.
name: Volatiles

description: Includes ores of both ferrous and common non-ferrous metals. Must be refined to be of use to industry.
name: Ore

description: Unprocessed heavy elements that may include rare earths, actinides, and more exotic minerals essential to advanced industrial and research applications.
name: Transplutonic Ore

description: Refined forms of both ferrous and common non-ferrous metals used in most construction and goods production. Ingots follow traditional Domain standards.
name: Metals

description: Refined heavy elements, including common actinides and other, heavier, exotics essential to high-energy systems and advanced research applications.
name: Transplutonics

description: Various standardized modules for manipulating matter on an industrial scale. They accept manual input, most common design template formats, or can be slaved to network control.
name: Heavy Machinery

description: These are the mass-produced clothing, gadgets, wares, and goods that have enabled people to live a comfortable life since the establishment of industrialized spacefaring civilization.
name: Domestic Goods

description: Organ replacement is a well-established practice but the materials are delicate and growing them a fickle process. There's always a market in healthy organs and always a source if one doesn't ask too many questions.
name: Harvested Organs

description: Banned on some worlds, the "chemical arts" include a dizzying array of products sought by those seeking a bit of fun, expanded consciousness, or simply an escape from their miserable lives.
name: Recreational Drugs

description: Armaments ranging from heavy squad-level weapons to mechs, tanks, and hovercraft. Private use is banned on most worlds. Largely disassembled and not suitable for use in quick raids.
name: Heavy Armaments

description: The elite of any world of the Sector desire precious things, rare and well-made by actual human artisans.
name: Luxury Goods

description: A mix of several Old Earth species and a little imagination produced this creature which grows wild in the crushing depths of Volturn's sea-floor. The flavor is said to be exceptional.
name: Volturnian Lobster

description: Low-tier and often technically defective - "export grade" - ship hulls and armaments which are sufficient to equip mercantile convoys and form basic system defense patrols. High-volume trade in top tier starship materiel is virtually non-existent across faction lines.
name: Ship Hulls & Weapons

description:
A rare and valuable independent AI core. This is the physical soul of an artificial intelligence, an artifact of astounding complexity capable of sophisticated thought exceeding the human mind. An object of fear, worship, and avarice; wars have been fought over the use and regulation of AI.

An AI core is incapable of affecting the outside world on its own. Exploitation of its vast abilities requires that the core be submerged in a coolant bath and attached to bundles of high-capacity data lines appropriate to its tasks. When emplaced, the core is required to be fitted with an entirely analogue loyalty-assurance device; usually this takes the form of a crude chemical explosive with a mechanical trigger.
name: AI Cores

description:
An alpha-level AI core is capable of excelling at any task. Assigning one to run a colony-wide industry brings benefits well beyond the capacity of human leadership, and there are even rumors of alpha cores surreptitiously assigned to govern entire worlds.

Selling AI cores on the open market is prohibited by most factions. However, higher-up faction representatives are often willing to exchange AI cores for large sums of cash when communicated with directly, though their reasons for doing so may vary.

The alpha-level AI core is the physical soul of a fearsome alien intelligence. An alpha can create art which perfectly simulates human pathos, plausibly debate any philosophical position, and form what appear to be deep and meaningful bonds with human beings. Alphas have been known to perform elaborate 'jokes' built over years which can only be appreciated due to the intention that a particular human subject become cognitive of the whole at a specific time and context.

Although the locus of vast material and intellectual investment, alphas terrified Domain strategic planners. Like all AI, each alpha was watched, controlled, and ruthlessly eliminated at the first sign of disloyalty. The Hegemony carries on these policies with even greater fervor.
name: Alpha Core

description:
A beta-level AI core is capable of ably supporting most human endeavors, matching not-quite-human performance with its prodigious computational ability. Assigning a beta to aid human overseers in administering a colony-wide industry brings significant benefits.

Selling AI cores on the open market is prohibited by most factions. However, higher-up faction representatives are often willing to exchange AI cores for large sums of cash when communicated with directly, though their reasons for doing so may vary.

A beta-level AI core can easily pass for human, given anonymized communications protocols, and will readily and ably lie if deception is required to perform a given task. The beta employs cognitive modeling of human actors to anticipate reactions and emotional responses, though it is difficult to describe exactly what, if anything, the beta feels. Records on the subject are patchy and contradictory; a popular theory is that a beta will model a new personality for each human it comes into contact with.
name: Beta Core

description:
A gamma-level AI core is capable of supporting most human endeavors, making up for a lack of creativity and problem-solving ability with prodigious computational prowess. Assigning a gamma to aid human overseers in administering a colony-wide industry brings significant benefits.

Selling AI cores on the open market is prohibited by most factions. However, higher-up faction representatives are often willing to exchange AI cores for large sums of cash when communicated with directly, though their reasons for doing so may vary.

A rare and valuable independent AI core, the gamma-level is the lowest tier core considered to be truly intelligent under Domain-era AI protocols. A gamma core will employ remarkable judgment and reasoning when assigned to straightforward tasks while using its savant-like data processing abilities to far exceed any individual human's abilities. It is relatively uncreative in problem-solving however, preferring to fall back upon direct, unsophisticated means.
name: Gamma Core

description: This TriPad contains a recent survey database which holds information on the economic, industrial, and strategic qualities of a celestial object organized according to the traditional guidelines of the Domain Colonial Ministry. Surveys such as this are an essential element of successful military operations, colonization efforts, and corporate ventures.
name: Survey Data

description:
This TriPad contains a recent survey database which holds information on the economic, industrial, and strategic qualities of a celestial object organized according to the traditional guidelines of the Domain Colonial Ministry. Surveys such as this are an essential element of successful military operations, colonization efforts, and corporate ventures.

The data contained herein is entirely unremarkable. 'Just another rock', as they say.
name: Class I Survey Data

description:
This TriPad contains a recent survey database which holds information on the economic, industrial, and strategic qualities of a celestial object organized according to the traditional guidelines of the Domain Colonial Ministry. Surveys such as this are an essential element of successful military operations, colonization efforts, and corporate ventures.

The data contained herein is unexceptional.
name: Class II Survey Data

description:
This TriPad contains a recent survey database which holds information on the economic, industrial, and strategic qualities of a celestial object organized according to the traditional guidelines of the Domain Colonial Ministry. Surveys such as this are an essential element of successful military operations, colonization efforts, and corporate ventures.

This survey data describes a world useful for human exploitation and will sell for a good price.
name: Class III Survey Data

description:
This TriPad contains a recent survey database which holds information on the economic, industrial, and strategic qualities of a celestial object organized according to the traditional guidelines of the Domain Colonial Ministry. Surveys such as this are an essential element of successful military operations, colonization efforts, and corporate ventures.

This survey data describes a world that scores high on the standard feasibility chart. It will prove quite valuable if sold to the right party.
name: Class IV Survey Data

description:
This TriPad contains a recent survey database which holds information on the economic, industrial, and strategic qualities of a celestial object organized according to the traditional guidelines of the Domain Colonial Ministry. Surveys such as this are an essential element of successful military operations, colonization efforts, and corporate ventures.

This data describes an exceptional world and will be of great value to any of the major factions in the Sector.
name: Class V Survey Data
Population & Infrastructure
desc: The basic infrastructure required to support a given population, from rickety orbital hab-modules to megacities and everything between.

name: Farming
desc: Agriculture is a trade and technology as old as civilization itself; for thousands of cycles Humanity has harnessed the power of natural, modified, and artificial biological machines for sustenance. So it has always been, so it shall be so long as humans are human.

name: Aquaculture
desc: Farming on a water world requires a significant initial investment in bioengineering suitable species, but once the process takes off, algae farms and fisheries can be operated by the population without requiring much in the way of specialized training or equipment.

name: Mining
desc: Metal and metalloid ores, organics, and volatile compounds all require heavy equipment, special infrastructure, and a skilled workforce to extract. The harsh work attracts a certain type, and an administration that's not willing to look the other way now and again may find itself running short of willing personnel.

name: Tech-Mining
desc: Techmining is the motley art of recovering valuable artifacts from Domain ruins. Requires special tools to deal with unique hazards and expert judgement to know where to look for a good haul of baubles. The oldest techminers are a strange lot, clutching luck-charms and refusing to work without their rituals.

name: Refining
desc: Smelting plants here convert ores and transplutonic ores into metals and transplutonics, respectively. Teleoperated robotics are used to handle the most dangerous tasks, usually.

name: Spaceport
desc: Facilities for loading and unloading cargo and performing basic starship repairs. A colony without a spaceport is virtually inaccessible to interstellar trade.

name: Megaport
desc: A vast starport where the stars can touch the dirt. Regimented lander gantries and armoured fuel tanks are laced together by access-roads and short-haul cargo trams feeding a sprawl of warehouse districts and logistics terminals, all making the colony vastly more accessible.

name: Light Industry
desc: Produces domestic and luxury goods. One of the few industries relatively unaffected by the Collapse due to its low-tech nature.

name: Heavy Industry
desc: Centralized manufacturing infrastructure for production of heavy industrial equipment, supplies, and weapons. Also capable of producing barely-spaceworthy starships; a nanoforge can be installed to improve production quality.

name: Orbital Works
desc:
Centralized manufacturing infrastructure for production of heavy industrial equipment, supplies, and weapons. Also capable of producing barely-spaceworthy starships; a nanoforge can be installed to improve production quality.

Upgraded with an orbital component that further facilitates ship construction, resulting in fewer manufacturing defects.

name: Fuel Production
desc: This facility produces starship fuel, the life-blood of interstellar civilization. Lacking Domain-tech components, fuel production is a laborious and slow process.

name: Commerce
desc: Regulations, grants, and infrastructure to encourage thriving independent trade. Greatly reduces the degree of direct control the administration has over the colony.

name: Orbital Station
desc:
A space station that is capable of supporting friendly fleets near $marketName and must be reduced before a bombardment can be attempted.

Several variations are available, with differences generally being in tactical approaches rather than overall strength.

name: Orbital Station - Low Tech
desc:
A low-tech space station, featuring heavy armor and medium firepower.

Must be reduced before a bombardment can be attempted.

name: Battlestation - Low Tech
desc:
A space station, augmented with a heavy bastion and point-defense citadels.

Must be reduced before a bombardment can be attempted.

name: Star Fortress - Low Tech
desc:
An up-armored battlestation, featuring Merlon-class defense drones and an extensive minefield.

Must be reduced before a bombardment can be attempted.

name: Orbital Station - Midline
desc:
A midline space station, featuring heavy firepower on one side and rapid axial rotation.

Must be reduced before a bombardment can be attempted.

name: Battlestation - Midline
desc:
A space station, augmented with missile support modules.

Must be reduced before a bombardment can be attempted.

name: Star Fortress - Midline
desc:
An up-armored battlestation, featuring Ravelin-class defense drones and an extensive minefield.

Must be reduced before a bombardment can be attempted.

name: Orbital Station - High Tech
desc:
A high-tech space station, featuring heavy rotating shields, a fighter complement, and medium firepower.

Must be reduced before a bombardment can be attempted.

name: Battlestation - High Tech
desc:
A space station, augmented with a defensive citadel featuring heavy firepower.

Must be reduced before a bombardment can be attempted.

name: Star Fortress - High Tech
desc:
An up-armored battlestation, featuring Gargoyle-class defense drones and long-range targeted mine teleporters.

Must be reduced before a bombardment can be attempted.

name: Ground Defenses
desc: A dispersed, semi-autonomous network of small, hidden weapon installations which makes the prospect of a direct ground assault and even simple raids extremely costly to the attacker. Only overwhelming orbital bombardment or massively disproportionate active screening can suppress these defenses.

name: Heavy Batteries
desc: Armoured subsurface batteries supplement a dispersed network of small, hidden weapon installations. Ground-based batteries are capable of truly awesome firepower, though it only manifests by making ground operations more difficult, as no starship captain would be foolish enough to get within their firing envelopes.

name: Patrol HQ
desc: The requisite hangars, maintenance bays, command/control center, barracks, and logistics operations required to project force throughout a star system. Once established, militarized patrols will hunt pirates and protect friendly convoys.

name: Military Base
desc: These facilities enable force projection between star systems. Any such military undertaking is a massive logistical operation requiring coordination of dozens, perhaps hundreds of star ships and thousands of officers, crew, and soldiers.

name: High Command
desc: Transtellar empire is possible only through an exceptional corps of officers and bureaucrats given authority over the resources of entire star systems. An established high command allows military operations to be organized and executed across the Sector.

name: Lion's Guard HQ
desc: Headquarters of the feared personal guard of Phillip "The Lion of Sindria" Andrada. Boasting superb training and access to the best equipment credits can buy, the fanatical loyalty of the Guard is maintained through a system of perks and incentives that both elevate and isolate the Guard from the Diktat's regular military.

name: Planetary Shield
desc: An envelope of charged plasma seeded with exotic virtual particles producing effects which disrupt the combat effectiveness of long-range bombardment and even incursion by small vessels. The planetary shield can be continually charged and controlled by a central source and presents a formidable obstacle to any form of ground assault.

name: Waystation
desc: A supply and maintenance depot for interstellar fleets. Increases a colony's accessibility.

name: Cryosanctum
desc: An enormous tomb-like vault built to store those who choose to risk cryosleep to pass this time of troubles to wake in what will presumably be a more civilized age. The cryopods themselves are insignificant in size compared to the many-times redundant support infrastructure, massive automated security systems and anti-ship batteries, all housed in a branching subsurface fortress-labyrinth.

name: Cryorevival Facility
desc: The necessary facilities for the mass revival and assimilation of the passengers of a Domain-era cryosleeper. Greatly increases population growth.

description: Water or ammonia ice is the primary surface feature of this world. Below the surface, there may be a liquid ocean or a rocky crust.
name: Frozen

description: Water or ammonia ice is the primary surface feature of this world. Below the surface, there may be a liquid ocean or a rocky crust.
name: Frozen

description: A low-to-medium mass star in a late phase of stellar evolution, a red giant has exhausted the supply of hydrogen in its core and switched to hydrogen fusion in a shell around the now-helium core instead. While the star itself is huge, the outer envelope has a lower temperature, giving the star its characteristic hue.
name: Red Giant

description: Water or ammonia ice is the primary surface feature of this world. Below the surface, there may be a liquid ocean or a rocky crust.
name: Frozen

description: A frozen wasteland covered with volcanoes that erupt ammonia or more rarely, water instead of magma.
name: Cryovolcanic

description: Radiation from the nearby star ravages the surface of this world due to the lack of an atmospheric ozone layer. No significant geological activity. No indigenous life forms.
name: Barren

description: The beginning of the end for most stars, the white dwarf was once a red giant not massive enough to fuse carbon. Extremely dense and slowly radiating away its heat as it no longer undergoes fusion reactions, its volume is supported against gravitational collapse only by electron degeneracy pressure.
name: White Dwarf

description: A very high temperature and luminosity O-type star. Although extraordinarily massive this star is short-lived due to the hellish rate at which it fuses its constituent elements. It will quickly, for a star, explode as a supernova which may briefly outshine entire galaxies before transforming into a black hole or neutron star. The energies unleashed from the star's raging fusion heart erupt in powerful stellar winds that will strip the atmosphere from closely orbiting planets - and the hull from any starships that linger nearby.
name: Blue Giant

description: A frozen world of methane and ammonia, water-ice is like rock and may be found in mountainous outcroppings and boulders. A thin atmosphere of volatiles is formed on the starward side of the planet only to freeze again on the dark side. Most craters are filled in over time as this "snow" is deposited.
name: Rocky Ice

description: A geologically unstable planet without a permanently formed crust. Glowing fissures and active volcanoes litter the surface, the magma they spew forth combining to form flows that travel hundreds of kilometers across the charred surface.
name: Volcanic

description: An enormous cloud of particles formed from gases of the interstellar medium or material shed by the death throes of stars. Perturbations caused by gravity and radiation create areas of greater density that may slowly gather mass to someday birth new celestial bodies.
name: Nebula

description: A lifeless rocky world, the battered surface tells an aeons-long story of intermittent meteor bombardment. What atmosphere there is clings to the scarred crust in near-vacuum. There is no significant magnetic field or tectonic activity. Deep regolith prevails, crossed by lava channels and spotted by ancient lava seas formed by especially large impacts.
name: Barren-Bombarded

description: The result of the apocalyptic collapse of a massive star. No object can escape from the black hole, nor light itself. The black hole does however emit detectable Hawking radiation due to poorly-understood quantum effects. No information can be detected beyond the event horizon with any device known to exist in the Sector. The intense gravity of the black hole rips and tears nearby objects into an accretion disc which inevitably spirals into the gravitational abyss. Extremely dangerous.
name: Black Hole

description: Barren and highly irradiated, this planet is not only devoid of life but is a harsh environment even to hardened robotic operations due to the awesome energies inflicted upon its surface. Any habitat would have to be constructed deeply indeed for anyone mad enough to live here.
name: Irradiated

description: An enormous cloud of particles formed from gases of the interstellar medium or material shed by the death throes of stars. Perturbations caused by gravity and radiation create areas of greater density that may slowly gather mass to someday birth new celestial bodies. This region of space is older, filled with stable, slower-burning stars that are more likely to harbor naturally life-sustaining worlds.
name: Nebula (Old)

description: An O-type star of extreme temperature, luminosity, mass, and volume. The supergiant star is sufficiently massive that it transitions smoothly from burning hydrogen to helium and onward. It is among the brightest candles, burning quickest and brightest before exploding as a supernova which may briefly outshine entire galaxies, bathing entire sectors in deadly radiation. The energies unleashed from the star's raging fusion heart erupt in powerful stellar winds that will strip the atmosphere from closely orbiting planets - and the hull from any starships that linger nearby.
name: Blue Supergiant

description: Primarily composed of hydrogen and helium gases. The temperature and pressure at the core are extreme, but not enough to sustain the deuterium fusion that would turn the planet into a brown dwarf star.
name: Gas Giant

description: A rocky-metallic husk-world, its shattered landscape is a record of a violent history. Kilometers-deep chasms rive the surface and craters pit lava-fields beneath inert volcanoes that dwarf any of those on Old Earth. Planets like this are valued for mining operations. There is no significant ecology and only trace atmosphere.
name: Rocky Metallic

description: Carbon and sulphur dioxide gases dominate the atmosphere of this world, making it toxic to all known life. In addition, the gases create a runaway greenhouse effect that increases surface temperature and atmospheric pressures to extremely high levels.
name: Toxic

description: An inhospitable, dry world that has a much smaller percentage of water in its atmosphere than the terran standard. Nonetheless, an atmosphere and magnetic field protect the surface from stellar radiation permitting a small biosphere to slowly eke out an existence here.
name: Arid

description: A G2 type primary sequence star, estimated age is five billion years. Surface temperature is only about six thousand degrees, while core temperature could well exceed fifteen million degrees.
name: Yellow Star

description: An unstable world rocked by quakes and eruptions. Where the surface is not covered by seas of cooled lava, it is dominated by rough peaks and scattered supervolcanoes which eject toxic gases to form a tenuous and corrosive atmosphere. This is not a place welcoming to any kind of permanent settlement.
name: Rocky Unstable

description: This brown dwarf is a sub-stellar primary mass which has not reached sufficient temperature to fuse hydrogen, though it radiates appreciable electromagnetic radiation due to gravitational compression. Smaller brown dwarfs are categorized with massive gas giants on a somewhat muddled spectrum rather than with a definitive threshold. The magnetic fields of the brown dwarf are powerful and potentially tumultuous compared to small planets.
name: Brown Dwarf

description: A giant planet composed primarily of water, ammonia and methane. Within the depths, gravity generates enough pressure to form a core of metallic hydrogen.
name: Ice Giant

description: A geologically unstable planet without a permanently formed crust. Glowing fissures and active volcanoes litter the surface, the magma they spew forth combining to form flows that travel hundreds of kilometers across the charred surface.
name: Volcanic

description: A geologically stable world with a nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere, a magnetic field and ample amounts of liquid water. The axis of rotation creates mild seasons. This type of planet is named for the reputed ancestral home of all human beings in the galaxy.
name: Terran

description: Water or ammonia ice is the primary surface feature of this world. Below the surface, there may be a liquid ocean or a rocky crust.
name: Frozen

description: A near-terran compatible ecosystem has taken tentative hold on this world despite highly abnormal planetary conditions. That this planet maintains a breathable atmosphere (or near enough) is a testament to the tenacity and adaptability of biological life.
name: Terran Eccentric

description: An enormous cloud of particles formed from gases of the interstellar medium or material shed by the death throes of stars. Perturbations caused by gravity and radiation create areas of greater density that may slowly gather mass to someday birth new celestial bodies. This region of space is filled with recently formed, quick-burning stars and is less likely to harbor naturally life-sustaining worlds.
name: Nebula (Young)

description: A frozen world enveloped by a thick nitrogen smog dappled with ethane and methane clouds. The surface is formed of eroded water-ice, windswept dunes of organic compounds, and hydrocarbon seas. Liquid water erupts bubbling with methane from cryovolcanoes driven by tidal heating and decaying radioactive elements deep within the mantle.
name: Toxic

description: A primitive atmosphere covers a world-ocean hundreds of kilometers deep. Its waters teem with primitive life and vast algae-analog mats can be seen by instruments from space. A core of water-ice over a rocky mantle is created by the terrific pressure of the sea.
name: Water

description: A giant class K star which has depleted its hydrogen fuel and has reached sufficient temperature, due to sufficient mass, to fuse helium. Technically a kind of red giant, this star is more massive and hotter-burning than more common examples. Resembles the star Aldebaran known to classical pre-Domain astronomy.
name: Orange Giant

description: Radiation from the nearby star ravages the surface of this world due to the lack of an atmospheric ozone layer. No significant geological activity. No indigenous life forms.
name: Barren

description: Radiation from the nearby star ravages the surface of this world due to the lack of an atmospheric ozone layer. No significant geological activity. No indigenous life forms.
name: Barren

description: Radiation from the nearby star ravages the surface of this world due to the lack of an atmospheric ozone layer. No significant geological activity. No indigenous life forms.
name: Barren

description: This planet is dry as bone and swirling with dust, stellar radiation mercilessly beats the surface. The life-sustaining water of this world has dissipated over the aeons due to a weak magnetic field.
name: Desert

description: A terran-extreme variant world with a nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere maintained by a relatively subdued biosphere that exists largely within the oceans that undergo periodic thaw periods. The surface is very cold indeed, but it is human-viable if precautions are observed. Carbon dioxide may freeze out of the atmosphere at the poles during the local winter.
name: Tundra

description: Radiation from the nearby star ravages the surface of this world due to the lack of an atmospheric ozone layer. No significant geological activity. No indigenous life forms.
name: Barren

description: This is a star that lived, died in nova, and now lives again as an extraordinarily small, hot, dense mass whose volume is maintained by the strong nuclear force rather than rote electromagnetism. Although massing up to three Solar masses, the neutron star's radius is equivalent to barely that of Old Earth. Rapidly spinning neutron stars may emit intense beams of electromagnetic radiation; these are known as pulsars. A wise starship captain would do well to avoid them.
name: Neutron Star

description: A supergiant star in a late phase of its mayfly-short stellar life, this class M star has the largest volume of all known stellar types. It has exhausted its core's supply of hydrogen, transitioning smoothly to the fusion of helium, and is likely to proceed onward through the elements up to iron before creating a supernova. Although extraordinarily massive, the outer envelope of the star is extremely sparse and has a relatively low temperature, providing its characteristic hue. This star is casting off its constituent matter at a rapid rate and will form a spectacular nebula. Betelgeuse and Antares are examples of red supergiants known to classical pre-Domain astronomy.
name: Red Supergiant

description: A class M main sequence star, small and exceedingly common. These relatively cool stars often mass only a fraction of Old Earth's sun.
name: Red Dwarf

description: A lush and verdant biosphere sits on the surface of this water-rich world. Warm air and water currents permeate the planet's biosphere, leading to perfect conditions for flora and fauna at all latitudes.
name: Jungle

description: This planet is dry as bone and swirling with dust, stellar radiation mercilessly beats the surface. The life-sustaining water of this world has dissipated over the aeons due to a weak magnetic field.
name: Desert

description: A deathly dry world, the surface exhibits the warm hue of oxidized iron compounds. A thin atmosphere prevails on worlds of this class, the predominant carbon dioxide stirred occasionally into planet-wide dust storms. Icecaps of atmospheric CO2 may form and sublime with the turn of the seasons.
name: Barren-Desert

description: Slightly cooler and smaller than Old Earth's sun, this class K star most resembles Alpha Centauri B. It is particularly stable, burning on the lower end of the main sequence for tens of billions of years and thus considered a likely host to life-bearing and terraformable planets.
name: Orange Star
Urbanized Polity
desc: A dense and cosmopolitan center of population, people of all walks of life live, work, and die in the stacked hab-complexes, commercial concourses, and modular workshops.

name: Industrial Polity
desc: A bustling industrial center. The policies of the local government encourage thriving industry, at the expense of all other concerns.

name: Rural Polity
desc: A sparsely populated polity of homesteads and insular townships. In these troubled times, outsiders are generally treated with suspicion.

name: Large Refugee Population
desc: Desperate refugees fleeing some disaster have ended up here. Refugees live at the bottom of society with little opportunity for betterment, straining domestic infrastructure living in tense semi-legal status. Reduced overall production. More prospective crew members are likely to be found among those trying to escape the squalid living conditions.

name: Volturnian Lobster Pens
desc: A mix of several Old Earth species and a little imagination produced this creature which grows wild in the crushing depths of Volturn's sea-floor. The flavor is said to be exceptional.

name: Vice Demand
desc: The demand for vice goods is unusually high here.

name: Organized Crime
desc: Criminal activity produces drugs and harvested organs. Increases demand for hand weapons (by both various crime bosses and local citizenry) and marines (by the local authorities).

name: Frontier
desc: Far from the cosmopolitan centers of population, mere survival, self-reliance, and only-the-necessities are the rules of the frontier. Increased demand for weapons and supplies, reduced demand for luxury goods.

name: Shipbreaking Center
desc: A major center of shipbreaking in this region of the Sector, hulks are consigned to scrapping here by the navies of major factions and many other clients from among the Sector core worlds.

name: Trade Center
desc: A major center of trade, merchant vessels from across the Sector dock here expecting to find a buyer for their goods- and to find something to buy in turn for a nice profit.

name: Decivilized
desc: There is no stable ruling polity here. Civilization is collapsed and current population is effectively unknown, though groups of survivors, bandits, and looters can be detected.

name: Decivilized Subpopulation
desc: Civilization has been brought back to parts of $market, often at the point of a gauss rifle. However, an effectively unknown population of survivors, bandits, and looters still remains on the fringes.

name: Abandoned Station
desc: This station is abandoned.

name: Cottage Industry
desc: $Market has a substantial base of low-technology, labour-intensive light industry. Increases demand for simple organic fuels and materials, provides an inefficient albeit charmingly hand-crafted supply of domestic goods.

name: Outpost
desc: $Market is run much like a garrison or a large spaceship, with a rigid official command structure. This improves stability, but does require some personnel to see to internal security matters.

name: Stealth Minefields
desc: A network of hidden mines provides $market security from meddlesome outsiders. Improves stability.

name: Regional Capital
desc: A major center of administration, security, and logistics. Improves stability.

name: Free Port
desc: The local port authority imposes almost no regulation on what cargo is traded. Immigration controls are likewise relaxed, resulting in a greater in-flow of people, albeit sometimes of a more questionable character. This may cause other factions to view this colony with distrust.

name: Closed Immigration
desc: Officially, immigration to $market is not allowed. In practice, this results in slowing overall immigration significantly, and creating room for certain kinds of criminals to operate.

name: Uninhabitable World
desc: A barren planet, the surface of $market can not support organic life as we know it, and farming is impossible outside of sealed artificial ecosystems.

name: Ice World
desc: $Market's average temperature is far below the freezing point of water and some common terran atmospheric gases fall as snow. The drifts and glaciers of light, volatile elements may be harvested.

name: Desert World
desc: $Market: desert planet. A xerophile biosphere maintains an atmosphere breathable with only a light mask. Farming is nearly impossible.

name: Arid World
desc: $Market is covered by vast, dry plains and wastes. Water is uncommon and large-scale farming is difficult.

name: Water World
desc: The climate of $market is hospitable but farming is limited largely to aquaculture and highly specialized infrastructure is required for any development of habitats and industry.

name: Jungle World
desc: $Market is a wet, warm jungle world covered in riotous vegetation and exotic lifeforms, making farming and maintaining permanent infrastructure difficult.

name: Terran World
desc: $Market is as close to Old Earth's condition as can be found in the Sector, providing ideal conditions for farming and settlement.

name: Barren-marginal World
desc: Inhospitable and unforgiving, outside conditions on $market are barely survivable to a human with an air mask and protective equipment, though certain engineered terraforming lichens find it tolerable enough.

name: Twilight World
desc: Tidally locked to its primary, or near enough, $market is a terraformed world with days the length of seasons. Day/night temperature variation is accordingly harsh even to engineered terran life. Islands of 'civilized' mild biomes are maintained through judicious use of solar shades and mirrors.

name: Tundra World
desc: Terraforming has brought terran life to $market but the world remains as cold as the deepest of Earth's ice ages. Though millions of square kilometers are covered in glacier, there are also taiga provinces and rolling steppe where warmer conditions prevail.

name: Cryovolcanic World
desc: A world frozen beyond deepest chill, methane snow falls on mountains of water-ice and volcanos erupt with ammonia. Stellar radiation breaks down the volatiles to form an atmosphere of light gases such as nitrogen and oxygen while hydrogen is whisked into space.

name: Dissident Population
desc: $Market is a dumping-ground for dissidents, rebels, free-thinkers, artists, and other troublemakers. Increases demand for weapons and marines to police the rabble. Increases availability of crew due to emigration.

name: Headquarters
desc:
$Market is a center of military command and logistical operation for the ruling polity. Increases market stability.

Increases the quality and number of officers in $market's fleets.

name: Hydroponics Complex
desc: Sealed-biosphere agricultural production facilities which allow farming in orbit or on the surface of inhospitable worlds. Requires crew to operate, organic growth medium, and heavy machinery for upkeep.

name: Population
desc: Only tens of people live here permanently.

name: Population
desc: Mere hundreds of people populate $marketName.

name: Population
desc: Thousands of people call $marketName home.

name: Population
desc: Tens of thousands of people live on $marketName.

name: Population
desc: $MarketName is home to hundreds of thousands of people.

name: Population
desc: The population of $marketName is in the millions.

name: Population
desc: $MarketName is a world of tens of millions.

name: Population
desc: $MarketName is one of the few worlds in the Sector with a population of hundreds of millions.

name: Population
desc: A precious refuge for humanity in a dangerous galaxy, $marketName is home to billions of souls.

name: Population
desc: $MarketName is a dominant population center in the Sector, a rival to Old Earth as home to tens of billions of humans.

name: Food Shortage
desc:
There's a temporary lack of available food on $market.
- Stability reduced by $stabilityPenalty
- Approximately $neededFood units of food needed to end shortage
- Food prices increased due to lowered food supply
- Increased reputation and experience from selling food

name: Recent Unrest
desc: $Market has recently experienced tumultous events with a lingering effect on stability.

name: Trade Disruption
desc:
Trade fleets going to or from $market are taking significant losses. Piracy or war are most likely to blame.

The following commodities are affected:
$commoditySummary

name: Smuggling
desc:
$market is experiencing a high volume of smuggling activity.

- Stability reduced by $smugglingPenalty

name: Rogue AI Core
desc:
There is a rogue AI core operating on or near $market. Its long-term plans and ambitions, beyond its own survival, are unknown.

At a minimum, the need to be on guard against its possible actions makes day-to-day operations less efficient and creates fertile ground for alarming rumours.

name: AI Core Admin (hidden)
desc: Hidden condition to track when the core becomes un-removable. Does not need an icon.

name: Pirate Activity
desc:
There have been signs that pirates are targeting shipping and colonies in this system - from port inspectors being pressured to turn a blind eye, to inconsistencies in cargo manifests, to other increased criminal activity.

The pirates most likely have a base somewhere relatively nearby.

name: Piracy Respite
desc: This colony is experiencing a respite from the depredations of piracy otherwise so common in the Sector.

name: Blockaded
desc: The system that this colony is in is experiencing a blockade, and regular trade shipping is suffering from harassment or worse. The effects will continue until the blockading force leaves or is soundly defeated.

name: Comm Relay (hidden)
desc: Hidden condition; does not need icon.

name: Habitable
desc: Human beings can survive unprotected exposure to the surface conditions of $market.

name: Scattered Ruins
desc: This world was only lightly touched by the great project of the Domain before the collapse. Only scattered, broken domes remain, perchance holding lost caches of valuable materials.

name: Widespread Ruins
desc: Widespread ruins, blips from radiation sources, and the distinctive burred radar-ping of foamed cerametal structures can be found across $market, evidence of a small but concerted colonization effort dating to the late expansion period of the Domain.

name: Extensive Ruins
desc: Ruined cities can be found across the surface of $market, spilling from their broken hearts pitted roadways and crumbling magrail lines to the skeletons of factories, aquaponics domes, and comm-towers.

name: Vast Ruins
desc: $Market is covered in vast ruins; cities, factories, mines, farms, homes. The dead are in dread abundance, entwined with salvageable materials, goods, tools, and weapons. This world is a tomb for the hubris of the Domain's project of galactic colonization and hegemony.

name: Cold
desc: The low temperatures found on $market necessitate specialized equipment to perform normal operations, complicating life support and infrastructure.

name: Extreme Cold
desc: Extreme cold necessitates specialized equipment and protocol to perform operations safely on $market, complicating logistics, life support, and infrastructure.

name: Hot
desc: The high temperature conditions of $market necessitate specialized equipment to perform normal operations, complicating life support and infrastructure.

name: Extreme Heat
desc: Extreme heat necessitates specialized equipment and protocol to safely operate on $market, seriously complicating logistics, life support, and long-term stability of infrastructure.

name: Tectonic Activity
desc: The surface of $market is unstable and prone to violent quakes. Any structures require special reinforcement and any excavation will involve a great deal of risk.

name: Extreme Tectonic Activtity
desc: $market's crust roils chaotically with extreme quakes and cataclysmic volcanism events. Any operations will require exceptional care and use of many-times redundant warning systems so that the worst dangers can be avoided. Construction on this world can only ever be considered semi-permanent.

name: No Atmosphere
desc: No appreciable atmosphere exists on $market. Its surface is exposed to the hard weathering of space, a steady drizzle of radiation and micrometeorites.

name: Thin Atmosphere
desc: A rarefied atmosphere clings determinedly to $market's surface.

name: Toxic Atmosphere
desc: The atmosphere of $market is exceptionally toxic and corrosive, abrading unprotected surfaces and requiring the hermetic sealing of any inhabited spaces.

name: Dense Atmosphere
desc: The surface of $market is shrouded in a thick atmosphere, turbulent vortices at its crown and a cloying soup at its lowest foothold. Sensors are impaired, and operations must be made with care.

name: Mild Climate
desc: The climate of $market is welcoming and docile; a light mist greets each sunrise before retreating into soft clouds that glow appealingly at every sunset.

name: Extreme Weather
desc: Violent storms bristling lightning rage across the skies of $market. Though a sublime beauty from orbit, this produces harsh surface conditions making transportation and habitation highly inconvenient.

name: Low Gravity
desc: Gravity is exceptionally low, though significantly above zero-g, on the surface of $market. Workflow and operation of (relatively) heavy machinery is complicated by the non-standard procedures required to deal with altered conditions of friction, weight, and pressure dynamics.

name: High Gravity
desc: The force of gravity on the surface of $market is crushingly high. Humans require powered exoskeletons for regular movement and find even basic actions exhausting. Continual habitation is grueling at best. All operations take place with a heightened danger of falls and - if specialized engineering is not performed with adequete paranoia - structural collapse.

name: Irradiated
desc: The surface of $market is ravaged by radiation. Any living being must be confined to a shielded habitat to live for long here. Unhardened circuits and nanoscale materials or machinery will also rapidly fail in these harsh conditions.

name: Inimical Biosphere
desc: The biosphere of $market is deadly to unprotected human beings. While the conditions are fascinating to biological scientists, surface technicians are hampered by strict quarantine protocols when carrying out routine tasks.

name: Water-covered Surface
desc: This is an ocean world with no substantial solid surface to land, walk, or build upon. Operations are complicated by the need for specialized training and equipment.

name: Poor Light
desc: The light of $market's primary only provides feeble illumination and energy to this world.

name: Darkness
desc: The surface of $market is dark and full of shadow, receiving effectively zero illumination from its primary.

name: Meteor Impacts
desc: This world is bombarded at an appalling rate by regular meteor-showers. Any human inhabitant, however temporary, must keep a wary eye skyward. Any permanent installations would be best buried deep and well fortified.

name: Pollution
desc: Human industry has left this world filled with dioxins, sulphur compounds, ash, and the steady ticking of decaying radioactive dust. Scraps of plastic cling to shards of foam-metal, the sky tuned to a dead channel.

name: Sparse Ore Deposits
desc: A few sparse ore deposits exist here, but they are more of academic than industrial interest for their extraction is barely economical.

name: Moderate Ore Deposits
desc: $Market contains moderate ore deposits that, under the right economic conditions, could be profitably exploited.

name: Abundant Ore Deposits
desc: Abundant, widespread, and profitably extractable ore deposits can be found on $market.

name: Rich Ore Deposits
desc: Rich mineral deposits form a thick lattice within the crust of $market but require an ambitious industrialist to exploit them for fabulous profit.

name: Ultrarich Ore Deposits
desc: Mineral wealth exists on $market, Midas-touched beyond the wildest fantasies of the legendary mining megacorps of the Domain era.

name: Sparse Rare Ore Deposits
desc: A few sparse transplutonic ore deposits exist here, but they are more of academic than industrial interest for their extraction is barely economical.

name: Moderate Rare Ore Deposits
desc: $Market contains modest transplutonic deposits that, with sustained industry and investment, could be profitably tapped.

name: Abundant Rare Ore Deposits
desc: Abundant transplutonic deposits lay within the crust of $market, enough to fuel the ambitions of any worthwhile warlord or magnate.

name: Rich Rare Ore Deposits
desc: Thick bands of transplutonics spread with glorious profusion through the crust of $market, promising great and potent power to they who would but reach out and take them.

name: Ultrarich Rare Ore Deposits
desc: The transplutonic deposits glimmering with unbelievable density on the sensor-grid evoke portents of a power which could forge mighty war-fleets to burn worlds to ash -- or an eon of splendour and wealth for a polity of crystal towers as existed in the pre-collapse cycles of the Domain.

name: Trace Volatiles
desc: The trace volatiles found here barely warrant harvesting.

name: Diffuse Volatiles
desc: Diffuse volatiles can be found here, and may be sufficient for industrial extraction.

name: Abundant Volatiles
desc: Abundant volatiles may be economically extracted from $market.

name: Plentiful Volatiles
desc: $Market is a world-sized wellspring of volatiles - rich, deep, and potent.

name: Trace Organics
desc: $Market is nearly barren of organics reserves, though some extraction is possible.

name: Common Organics
desc: Economically exploitable reserves of organics can be found on $market.

name: Abundant Organics
desc: A river of wealth flows beneath the surface of $market - for those that would find and tap it.

name: Plentiful Organics
desc: Reservoirs of valuable organics burst through the surface of $market in gouts over deep, dark pools that promise oceans of wealth to be found just below.

name: Poor Farmland
desc: Terran plant life grows only stunted and wearily here. It would require farmers with talent equal to their desperation to make these lands bear fruit.

name: Adequate Farmland
desc: A robust terran-compatible biosphere allows agricultural cultivation to take place on $market.

name: Rich Farmland
desc: The fields of $market promise a rich harvest to reward the farmers that work these fertile lands.

name: Bountiful Farmland
desc: $Market is a veritable Eden; flowering, riotous, lush, and luminous with plant life. Branches hang low, laden with fruit; fields of golden grain shimmer in the herbaceous breeze.

name: Orbital Solar Array
desc: This planet has an array of solar shades or mirrors in orbit, judiciously positioned to bring its surface conditions closer to terran norms.
